cues.en: Okay. So here's the damn deal. Back in 2007, I wrote three freelance articles for a tech news website. The premise was I spent days working with each of the operating systems that were out at the time, Ubuntu six, Mac OS 10.4,
cues.zh: 好的，事情是这样的。2007年，我给一家科技新闻网站写了三篇自由撰稿文章。前提是，我花好几天时间逐一使用当时已有的每个操作系统：Ubuntu 6、Mac OS 10.4，

cues.en: and Windows Vista. I couldn't just use the operating system for an hour or two, take some notes, move on. No. The purpose of the project was to find out if all these operating systems could be used day to day. I would even write the articles on the computers I was using to review the operating systems.
cues.zh: 以及 Windows Vista。我不能只是用一两个小时操作系统、记点笔记就走。不行。这个项目的目的，是弄清这些操作系统是否都能日常使用。我甚至会在用来评测这些操作系统的电脑上写文章。

cues.en: So, anyway, I took a few full time jobs after that, but now it's 2012. I'm a freelancer again, and Microsoft has just released a new version of Windows. I figure, what the hell? Why not do the same thing? Spend thirty days or so with Windows eight, make some notes, sell the result. What could go wrong?
cues.zh: 后来我又做了几份全职工作，但到了2012年，我又成了自由职业者，而微软刚发布了新版 Windows。我心想，管他呢，为什么不照做一遍？花三十天左右用 Windows 8，做点记录，再把成果卖掉。能出什么问题呢？

cues.en: Well, as it turns out, just about everything.
cues.zh: 结果呢，几乎什么都出了问题。

cues.en: See, and I don't use this term as hyperbole. Windows eight is unusable.
cues.zh: 听着，我用这个词可不是夸张。Windows 8 根本没法用。

cues.en: And by that, I don't mean that I personally didn't like it or I wasn't used to the conventions of the operating system and preferred the old Windows seven. No. What I mean by unusable
cues.zh: 我说它不能用，并不是说我个人不喜欢它，或者不习惯这个操作系统的习惯用法、更偏爱老版 Windows 7。不是的。我说的“不能用”

cues.en: is that ultimately, the operating system was so poorly designed that it presented unsurmountable
cues.zh: 是指这个操作系统的设计实在太糟糕，带来了无法逾越的

cues.en: problems which prevented me from actually getting my work done. If Windows eight was a car, the radio would deafen you the second you started it. There wouldn't be a steering wheel, and for some reason, there'd be an ejector seat that goes off every five minutes.
cues.zh: 问题，让我根本没法完成工作。如果 Windows 8 是一辆车，你一启动，收音机就会把你震聋。车上没有方向盘，而且不知为何，还装了个每五分钟就弹射一次的弹射座椅。

cues.en: Now Microsoft claims that the new operating system was more user friendly,
cues.zh: 微软声称新操作系统更加用户友好，

cues.en: but this is the first operating system I've ever had to deal with that I could accurately and honestly call user hostile.
cues.zh: 但这是我接触过的第一个我能准确而诚实地说它敌视用户的操作系统。

cues.en: So I have, like, a ton of tests I was planning to do on this thing. I was planning to test the boot up times, benchmark tests, torture tests. I mean, I was gonna do some serious science in Windows eight.
cues.zh: 我原本打算在这上面做一大堆测试。我计划测试启动时间、基准测试、折磨测试。我是说，我准备在Windows 8上做些严肃的科学研究。

cues.en: And you know what? I'll I'll just give Microsoft all that as a freebie. I didn't get to see it for myself, but sure. Let's just say that Windows eight is faster than Windows seven. It doesn't matter how fast something is if you can't use it.
cues.zh: 你知道吗？我就把这些当作免费赠品送给微软了。我自己没能亲眼看到，但好吧。就假设Windows 8比Windows 7快吧。但如果一个东西你根本用不了，它有多快都无所谓。

cues.en: See, there's a couple of key things which you have to take into consideration when developing
cues.zh: 你看，开发时有几个关键因素你必须考虑

cues.en: interface, especially an operating system user interface because that's, like, the main thing that people are going to be interacting with on their computers.
cues.zh: 界面，尤其是操作系统的用户界面，因为那基本上就是人们在电脑上主要打交道的东西。

cues.en: If an application's UI is bad, well, that sucks, but it just ruins the application.
cues.zh: 如果一个应用的 UI 很糟，那确实很糟糕，但毁掉的只是这个应用。

cues.en: But if an operating system's UI is bad, it ruins all the applications.
cues.zh: 但如果操作系统的 UI 很糟，那它会毁掉所有应用。

cues.en: And those key things are control,
cues.zh: 这些关键要素是控制、

cues.en: conveyance, continuity,
cues.zh: 引导性、连续性，

cues.en: and context.
cues.zh: 以及上下文。

cues.en: That is an operating system should feel like it gives you control.
cues.zh: 也就是说，操作系统应该让人感觉它把控制权交给了你。

cues.en: You should be able to tell it what to do and how. It should never feel like it's acting on its own or it's out of control.
cues.zh: 你应该能告诉它做什么、怎么做。它绝不该让人觉得它在自作主张，或者已经失控。

cues.en: It should also have good conveyance. You should be able to easily figure out where you need to go and what you need to do in order to accomplish
cues.zh: 它还应该有良好的引导性。你应该能轻松弄清自己该去哪里、该做什么，才能完成

cues.en: your task even if you've never done that task before.
cues.zh: 你的任务，哪怕你以前从没做过那件事。

cues.en: It needs to be continuous. It needs to have continuity.
cues.zh: 它必须是连续的。它必须具有连续性。

cues.en: If you're doing one action, pressing a key, moving a mouse, whatever does something, you want that same action to do the same thing across the entire operating system.
cues.zh: 如果你做一个操作，比如按键、移动鼠标，或任何会产生效果的动作，你会希望同一个操作在整个操作系统中的效果一致。

cues.en: Finally, it needs a good grasp of context.
cues.zh: 最后，它需要很好地把握上下文。

cues.en: You should be able to understand what things do simply by looking at them at a glance.
cues.zh: 你应该一眼就能明白各个东西是做什么的。

cues.en: Now there's always exceptions to the rule, but for the most part, every operating system has improved on their predecessors
cues.zh: 当然，总有例外，但大多数情况下，每个操作系统都在这些方面比前代有所改进

cues.en: from version to version in these four areas.
cues.zh: 从一个版本到下一个版本，在这四个方面。

cues.en: And even the earliest operating systems
cues.zh: 就连最早的操作系统

cues.en: at least, you know, paid some attention to it. I mean, look at DOS.
cues.zh: 至少也多少关注过这一点。我是说，看看 DOS。

cues.en: I mean, it's a command line, but even then you can see how the designers of DOS did their best to include the four c's. First, control.
cues.zh: 它是个命令行界面，但即便如此，你也能看出 DOS 的设计者是如何尽力融入那四个 C 的。首先是 Control（控制）。

cues.en: DOS doesn't do anything until you type a command in, and then it does exactly what you tell it to do.
cues.zh: DOS 在你输入命令之前什么都不做，然后它完全按照你的指令行事。

cues.en: Conveyance. Okay. Maybe you gotta type in c d backslash dash
cues.zh: Conveyance（传达）。好吧，也许你得输入 c d 反斜杠 短横

cues.en: caret whatever. But look, right there in the command prompt, it tells you exactly where you are. And with the d I r command, it gives you a list of places you could go to and files you could access.
cues.zh: caret 之类的。但你看，命令提示符里就明明白白告诉你自己现在在哪儿。而用 d i r 命令，它会列出你可以去的地方和可以访问的文件。

cues.en: Now context and continuity for DOS were difficult. You could only operate DOS if you knew the specific command that you wanted to do. And since DOS was only really a bare bones operating system, each program did things in different ways. WordPerfect had completely different controls from Lotus one two three, for example.
cues.zh: 当年 DOS 的上下文和连续性都很差。你必须知道要执行的具体命令，才能操作 DOS。而且 DOS 其实只是个极其简陋的操作系统，每个程序做事的方式都不一样。比如，WordPerfect 的操作方式和 Lotus 1-2-3 完全不同。

cues.en: But you know what? Things got better. Windows 3.1.
cues.zh: 但你猜怎么着？情况变好了。Windows 3.1。

cues.en: Bam. You've got better context. You can see a bunch of things you can do right there on the screen. You don't have to memorize the commands.
cues.zh: 砰。上下文更好了。你能直接在屏幕上看到一堆可做的操作。不用再死记命令了。

cues.en: And everything kinda works the same way. You click the icon to start the program. You click the little dash thing in the corner in order to close the program. Sure. Windows 3.1 is dated by today's standards, but even back then, Microsoft really was thinking about how to address the four c's.
cues.zh: 所有东西的运作方式都差不多。点图标启动程序，点角落里那个小横杠就关闭程序。当然，按今天的标准，Windows 3.1 已经过时了，但即便在当时，微软也真的在思考如何应对四个 C。

cues.en: Windows eight really screws up on all four.
cues.zh: Windows 8 把这四点全搞砸了。

cues.en: I mean, I never thought I'd say this, but they actually created an operating system less user friendly than DOS.
cues.zh: 我是说，我从没想过自己会说出这种话，但他们确实做出了一个比 DOS 还不友好的操作系统。

cues.en: When I first started up Windows eight, the first big problem, the one that really created the bulk of my aggravation with this OS, I didn't have any control over it. I mean this. The thing would just do things, and I had no idea how or even if I was causing it to do those things. I'd be trying to look up the solution to a problem, and all of a sudden the weather application would pop up. Now I didn't wanna bring up the weather in the first place, but I mean this wasn't like a situation where I could just say, oh, I know what idea there to cause that and I won't do that again. No. This just kept happening, and I had no freaking idea why.
cues.zh: 当我第一次启动 Windows 8 时，第一个大问题——也是这个系统真正给我带来大部分烦恼的问题——是我完全控制不了它。我是认真的。它想干什么就干什么，我根本不知道是怎么发生的，甚至不知道是不是我引起的。我正想查某个问题的解决办法，天气应用突然就弹出来了。首先我根本就没想打开天气，而且这不是那种我可以直接说“哦，我知道是哪个操作导致的，我以后不这么干就行了”的情况。不是的。它就一直这样，而我完全搞不懂为什么。

cues.en: It's like, don't know, you're trying to type an essay on how many ninjas it would take to defeat Godzilla or whatever.
cues.zh: 就像，不知道，你正试着打一篇论文，讨论要多少个忍者才能打败哥斯拉之类的。

cues.en: And all of a sudden, whoosh, a goblin appears in midair, farts in your face, and disappears. You think, what the what
cues.zh: 突然，“嗖”地一下，一只哥布林出现在半空中，冲你脸上放了个屁，然后消失了。你心想：这到底

cues.en: the fuck was that?
cues.zh: 他妈是怎么回事？

cues.en: And so after a while, you just go to back to work on your essay, and and and then it happens again.
cues.zh: 于是过了一会儿，你只好回去继续写论文，然后、然后、然后它又发生了。

cues.en: The goblin comes up and he farts in your face.
cues.zh: 那只哥布林冒出来，又冲你脸上放了个屁。

cues.en: And you know it's gonna happen again and again, but you have no idea when or why that goblin's gonna come back. And so after a while, you're thinking more about trying to brace yourself for the next goblin fart, which you can't predict, rather than your essay, which you're trying to work on.
cues.zh: 你知道这事会一遍又一遍发生，但你完全不知道那只哥布林什么时候、为什么会回来。于是过了一会儿，你更多是在想着怎么为下一次哥布林放屁做好准备——而那根本没法预测——而不是在写你本来要写的论文。

cues.en: Throws off your concentration is what I'm getting at here. To make things worse, Microsoft made two big design decisions,
cues.zh: 我想说的是，这会让你分心。更糟的是，微软做了两个重大设计决策，

cues.en: bad design decisions for their metro apps. First, they made these apps full screen.
cues.zh: 对他们的 Metro 应用来说，是糟糕的设计决策。首先，他们把这些应用做成了全屏。

cues.en: So, again, I'm trying to do something and the weather pops up and it completely obliterates
cues.zh: 所以，我又在试着做点事，天气弹了出来，彻底毁掉

cues.en: anything to do with anything I actually wanted to do.
cues.zh: 和我真正想做的事有关的一切。

cues.en: Say what you will about pop ups. They may be annoying, but at least they don't cover up everything when they do occur.
cues.zh: 随便你怎么说弹窗。它们可能很烦，但至少出现时不会遮住一切。

cues.en: The other problem was that I couldn't figure out a single way to close the damn weather application.
cues.zh: 另一个问题是，我根本找不到任何办法关掉这个该死的天气应用。

cues.en: There's no x in the corner. There's no instructions. No menu. How do I get rid of the damn thing?
cues.zh: 角落里没有叉号，没有说明，没有菜单。我到底该怎么把这个鬼东西弄掉？

cues.en: Even trying the usual things, right clicking, whatever, I couldn't get rid of it. I had absolutely no control over anything the computer was doing, and this was happening about once every minute and a half.
cues.zh: 连常规操作都试过了，右键单击什么的，还是关不掉。我对电脑正在做的事完全没有任何控制权，而这大概每一分半钟就会发生一次。

cues.en: I mean, how insignificant
cues.zh: 我是说，这会让用户感到多微不足道

cues.en: and hurt can that make a user feel?
cues.zh: 又多受伤？

cues.en: I know I felt powerless.
cues.zh: 我知道，我当时感到无能为力。

cues.en: Not just powerless, downright abused.
cues.zh: 不只是无能为力，简直是被虐待。

cues.en: After a while, I was begging and pleading Windows eight to stop. Oh, please.
cues.zh: 过了一阵，我苦苦哀求 Windows 8 停下来。求你了。

cues.en: Please, Windows eight. Please. I promise I won't do those things that make you hurt me again if you just tell me what those are. But Windows eight was like, no, for I am a capricious and jealous god. Now if you excuse me, I'm going to rape your dog and make you watch, and there's nothing you can do about it.
cues.zh: 求你了，Windows 8。求你了。只要你告诉我哪些事会让你伤害我，我保证不再做。但 Windows 8 却说：不行，因为我是个任性又善妒的神。现在失陪了，我要强暴你的狗，还逼你看着，而你无能为力。

cues.en: I think a big part of the lack of control was the decision to include swipe gestures into Windows eight.
cues.zh: 我觉得失控感很大程度上源于把滑动手势加进 Windows 8 的决定。

cues.en: One of those swipe gestures and the one that was causing me all these problems was that you can switch applications
cues.zh: 其中有一个滑动手势，也正是给我带来所有这些问题的那个，就是你可以切换应用

cues.en: by
cues.zh: 通过

cues.en: swiping your finger from the left edge of the touchpad to the right.
cues.zh: 手指从触控板左边缘向右滑动。

cues.en: The problem was there's absolutely no difference between the movement that someone would use
cues.zh: 问题在于，人们用来

cues.en: to swipe
cues.zh: 滑动

cues.en: and the movement that someone would use to move the cursor to the to the right. I mean, it it
cues.zh: 的动作，和人们用来把光标向右移的动作，完全没有区别。我是说，这这

cues.en: it it... It's the same movement.
cues.zh: 这这……完全是同一个动作。

cues.en: See, I'm using a touch pad on a laptop, and Windows treats the touch pad on a laptop
cues.zh: 你看，我在笔记本上用触控板，而 Windows 对待笔记本触控板的方式，

cues.en: the way it would treat a touchscreen on a tablet. But the problem is these are completely different interfaces that are used in completely different ways.
cues.zh: 跟对待平板触屏是一样的。但问题在于，这完全是两种不同的交互界面，使用方式也完全不同。

cues.en: When you use a tablet touchscreen, your are more or less absolute.
cues.zh: 用平板触屏时，你的操作多少是绝对定位的。

cues.en: That means if you wanna get up to a button on the screen, you just put your finger on that button. You don't need to move a cursor. You don't even have a cursor on a tablet. The position of your finger and the position of the input are exactly the same. So when you're telling the computer to do something
cues.zh: 也就是说，如果你想点到屏幕上的某个按钮，直接把手指放在那个按钮上就行。不需要移动光标，平板上甚至根本没有光标。你手指的位置和输入的位置完全一致。所以当你让电脑做事时

cues.en: by touching it on a touch screen tablet,
cues.zh: 通过在触屏平板上点它，

cues.en: you are sending information about position.
cues.zh: 你发出的是关于位置的信息。

cues.en: A touch pad on the other hand is used exactly like a mouse would be. You provide a relative direction to move a cursor.
cues.zh: 而触摸板用起来跟鼠标一模一样。你给出的是相对方向，让光标移动。

cues.en: Through the touchpad, you don't give any information to the computer about the position of the cursor, only the relative direction,
cues.zh: 通过触摸板，你并没有告诉电脑任何关于光标位置的信息，只给了相对方向、

cues.en: acceleration,
cues.zh: 加速度，

cues.en: and distance to move the cursor from its current position.
cues.zh: 以及让光标从当前位置移动的距离。

cues.en: To visualize this, let's say that you had a drawing application and the cursor is starting on the left edge of the canvas.
cues.zh: 为了直观理解这一点，假设你打开一个绘图应用，光标一开始位于画布的左边缘。

cues.en: If you use a touchscreen and you draw from either the left edge to the middle, through the middle, or from the middle to the right, you produce three different outputs.
cues.zh: 如果你使用触摸屏，从左边缘画到中间、穿过中间，或者从中间画到右边，会产生三种不同的输出。

cues.en: But when you use a touch pad or or a mouse for that matter, all three of those movements are going to produce the same exact thing.
cues.zh: 但如果你用触控板，或者鼠标，这三种动作都会产生完全相同的结果。

cues.en: So, apparently, when I was simply moving the cursor the way that I've been doing so on a typical touch pad, sometimes I was actually moving the mouse, and sometimes I'd be too close to the edge, and instead it would register as a swipe.
cues.zh: 所以，显然，当我只是像平时在普通触控板上那样移动光标时，有时我其实是在移动鼠标，有时又太靠近边缘，结果反而被识别成了滑动。

cues.en: Now I didn't have any context clues to tell me that that was what was happening, so I thought, well, what's going on? Is this swiping because I'm actually using two fingers, or am I holding down the button or something? I never did figure this one out on my own. I have to eventually look it up on the Logitech website
cues.zh: 我当时没有任何上下文线索能告诉我到底发生了什么，所以我就想，怎么回事？这是因为我真的用了两根手指才触发的滑动，还是我按住了按键之类的？我自己始终没弄明白这一点。最后我只好去 Logitech 网站上查

cues.en: on a different computer running Windows seven, by the way, because I couldn't get the thing to stop swiping long enough to search for answers to my problems.
cues.zh: 顺带一提，是在另一台运行 Windows 7 的电脑上查的，因为我根本没法让这东西停止滑动足够久，好去搜索解决我问题的答案。

cues.en: Another big problem with Windows eight was conveyance.
cues.zh: Windows 8 的另一个大问题是它的交付方式。

cues.en: Now as my first task, I wanted to take my new laptop and create a Windows installer disc. You see, it didn't come with one, and I intended to swap out the hard drive for an SSD for the performance test that I never got to run.
cues.zh: 现在，我的第一个任务是想用我的新笔记本电脑制作一张 Windows 安装光盘。你看，它没有附带安装盘，而我打算把硬盘换成 SSD，用来做那个我一直没能跑成的性能测试。

cues.en: See,
cues.zh: 你看，

cues.en: I wanted to give Windows eight the best, you know, possible shot, so I didn't want the hard drive to slow it down, be the bottleneck.
cues.zh: 我想给 Windows 8 尽可能最好的机会，你懂的，所以我不想让硬盘拖慢它、成为瓶颈。

cues.en: Anyway, in order to do this, I needed to create some way to install Windows eight from a DVD.
cues.zh: 总之，要做到这一点，我得想办法用 DVD 安装 Windows 8。

cues.en: I also wanted to make sure that there were no third party programs which could have affected the performance, and that also requires a clean install.
cues.zh: 我还想确保没有任何第三方程序会影响性能，而这也需要一次干净安装。

cues.en: But I didn't have the option of downloading an ISO or disk image and using the product key that would normally be found on a little sticker on the bottom of the computer because there was no sticker and there was no product key.
cues.zh: 但我没法选择下载 ISO 或磁盘镜像，再用通常贴在电脑底部小标签上的产品密钥——因为既没有标签，也没有产品密钥。

cues.en: Seriously,
cues.zh: 说真的，

cues.en: who at Microsoft approved that?
cues.zh: 微软到底是谁批准的这个？

cues.en: So how did I create the recovery disk? I didn't. I couldn't figure it out.
cues.zh: 那我是怎么创建恢复盘的？我没创建。我搞不明白。

cues.en: Now I could create what they called a repair disk, which would boot up a bare bones Windows something so that you could restore a disk image from a hidden partition on the hard drive, which by the way would be useless if you're replacing the hard drive or your master boot record got overwritten by a virus or you screwed up a Linux installation,
cues.zh: 现在我可以创建他们所谓的修复盘，它会启动一个精简版 Windows 之类的东西，让你能从硬盘上的隐藏分区恢复磁盘映像；不过顺带一提，如果你要更换硬盘，或者主引导记录被病毒覆盖，或者你把 Linux 安装搞砸了，这玩意儿就没用了，

cues.en: whatever.
cues.zh: 管他呢。

cues.en: But I couldn't figure out how to create an install disk.
cues.zh: 但我搞不懂怎么制作安装盘。

cues.en: I looked in the control panel and there was not... Actually, you know what? Let me back up here. At first, I couldn't figure out how to get to the control panel.
cues.zh: 我在控制面板里找过，但里面没有……其实，你知道吗？让我退一步说。一开始，我搞不懂怎么进入控制面板。

cues.en: The control panel is now an icon in the desktop folder,
cues.zh: 控制面板现在只是桌面文件夹里的一个图标，

cues.en: but it doesn't actually show up on the desktop.
cues.zh: 但它实际上并不会显示在桌面上。

cues.en: So I have trouble figuring out how to get to the control panel just to see if the solution to what I wanted was in the control panel. So I'd open up explorer. I'd have to somehow
cues.zh: 所以，我很难搞明白该怎么进入控制面板，只是为了看看我想要的解决方案是否就在控制面板里。于是我会打开资源管理器。我还得不知怎么地

cues.en: know to navigate to the desktop folder.
cues.zh: 知道要导航到桌面文件夹。

cues.en: And a few clicks later, find the icon to the control panel where you obviously don't expect it to be because
cues.zh: 再点几下，找到控制面板图标——它显然在你意想不到的位置，因为

cues.en: everything on the desktop is supposed be in the desktop folder and vice versa,
cues.zh: 桌面上的所有东西本应放在桌面文件夹里，反之亦然，

cues.en: and it's not on the desktop, but it is in the desktop folder.
cues.zh: 而它不在桌面上，却在桌面文件夹里。

cues.en: I mean, compare that to Windows seven. Start.
cues.zh: 我是说，跟 Windows 7 比一比。开始。

cues.en: Control panel.
cues.zh: 控制面板。

cues.en: Period.
cues.zh: 句号。

cues.en: Anyway, my solution to the recovery disk problem wasn't there in the control panel. I never did succeed at it. Now I talked to some other people who use Windows eight and apparently you have to open up the charms bar, something that there's no clue on how to do. You apparently drag the mouse to the corner and hold it there or something, something I wouldn't have guessed in a million years. You can also open it up by hitting the Windows key plus c, but no one uses the freaking Windows key. And besides, unless you knew specifically
cues.zh: 总之，我解决恢复磁盘问题的方法不在控制面板里。我始终没成功。后来我跟一些用 Windows 8 的人聊过，显然你得打开 charms bar，可完全看不出该怎么操作。显然要把鼠标拖到角落并停在那里之类的，这种事我一百万年也猜不到。也可以按 Windows 键加 C 打开，但没人会用那该死的 Windows 键。再说，除非你明确知道

cues.en: that it was called the charms bar,
cues.zh: 它叫 Charms 栏，

cues.en: would you even think you'd bring it up with c?
cues.zh: 你会想到用 c 来唤出它吗？

cues.en: Maybe with s because it looks like a freaking sidebar, and sidebar
cues.zh: 也许会想到用 s，因为它看起来就像个该死的侧边栏，而 sidebar

cues.en: starts with s.
cues.zh: 是以 s 开头的。

cues.en: Also,
cues.zh: 而且，

cues.en: the charms bar animation comes in from the side.
cues.zh: Charms 栏的动画是从侧边滑入的。

cues.en: So you'd expect to bring it up, you drag the mouse to the side.
cues.zh: 所以你会以为，要唤出它，就该把鼠标拖到侧边。

cues.en: Instead, you have to drag the mouse to the corner. Now if the animation came in from the corner, then I might be able to think, oh, so that might be where I drag the mouse to get to the charms bar. But no.
cues.zh: 但实际却得把鼠标拖到角落。要是动画从角落滑入，我可能还会想：哦，那也许就该把鼠标拖到那儿来打开 Charms 栏。可并不是。

cues.en: That's just another example of how bad the conveyance is.
cues.zh: 这又是一个说明传达方式有多糟糕的例子。

cues.en: So anyway, you open up the charms bar, click on search, type in recovery,
cues.zh: 总之，你打开超级按钮栏，点击搜索，输入 recovery，

cues.en: and it's not in apps. It's in settings.
cues.zh: 但它不在应用里。它在设置里。

cues.en: Settings,
cues.zh: 设置，

cues.en: which is normally a blank screen when you click on it with nothing typed in the search bar. Why?
cues.zh: 通常你点进去、搜索栏里什么都没输的时候，它就是一块空白屏幕。为什么？

cues.en: Apps isn't a blank screen when you click on it and type nothing.
cues.zh: 应用你点进去什么都不输，可不是空白屏幕。

cues.en: Anyway, you have to type in specifically
cues.zh: 总之，你必须专门输入

cues.en: recovery and you have to know specifically to search for that word recovery.
cues.zh: recovery，而且你必须明确知道要搜 recovery 这个词。

cues.en: Searches such as Windows disk, reinstall disk, reformat disk, clean install,
cues.zh: 像 Windows disk、reinstall disk、reformat disk、clean install 这样的搜索，

cues.en: none of them bring this up. So right there, you're back in the old days of DOS where you had to memorize the specific specific command in order to get something done.
cues.zh: 它们都没提到这个。所以就在这一点上，你仿佛回到了 DOS 时代，必须记住那个具体命令才能把事做成。

cues.en: Anyway, I wasn't able to figure this out on my own, which, you know, is is kind of a big deal. To put this into perspective, I taught myself Linux back when the most user friendly distribution was Slackware.
cues.zh: 总之，我自己没能弄明白这一点，你知道，这可不是小事。这么说吧，我自学 Linux 的时候，最友好的发行版还是 Slackware。

cues.en: I'm able to use, like, four or five different operating systems, can even find my way around a command line with some ability, so I'm not dumb.
cues.zh: 我能用大概四五种不同的操作系统，甚至还能比较熟练地在命令行里操作，所以我不笨。

cues.en: I'm not computer illiterate.
cues.zh: 我不是电脑文盲。

cues.en: When I can't find my way around an operating system, what hope do grandma and grandpa have?
cues.zh: 连我在某个操作系统里都摸不着北，爷爷奶奶还能有什么指望？

cues.en: Really,
cues.zh: 真的，

cues.en: really bad conveyance.
cues.zh: 传达性真的非常差。

cues.en: Now I think one of the reasons why conveyance is so poor is because Windows eight isn't really one user interface. It's two. They kind of stapled this new metro user interface over the old desktop type model.
cues.zh: 我觉得传达性这么差的原因之一，是 Windows 8 其实不算一个用户界面。它是两个。他们算是把这个新的 Metro 用户界面硬贴在了旧的桌面式模型上面。

cues.en: So there are two rules for everything. There's the rules of the old desktop
cues.zh: 所以每件事都有两套规则。一套是旧桌面的规则

cues.en: and the rules of the new metro user interface,
cues.zh: 另一套是新 Metro 用户界面的规则

cues.en: and they don't play well together.
cues.zh: 而它们配合得并不好。

cues.en: This is a complete lack of continuity.
cues.zh: 这完全缺乏连续性。

cues.en: The way you close applications in the desktop is to hit the little x in the corner. The way you close applications in Metro is...
cues.zh: 在桌面里关闭应用，是点角落里的小 x。而在 Metro 里关闭应用的方式是……

cues.en: You know what? Actually, I never figured out how to close applications in Metro.
cues.zh: 说实话，我其实一直没搞明白怎么在 Metro 里关闭应用。

cues.en: Anyway, desktop apps start in a window and can be moved around the screen. Metro apps are all full screen.
cues.zh: 桌面应用会以一个窗口启动，还能在屏幕上四处移动。Metro 应用则全是全屏的。

cues.en: Desktops apps generally have menus in the same place, they usually start the same way too. File, edit, etcetera.
cues.zh: 桌面应用的菜单通常都在同一个位置，启动方式也差不多，都是文件、编辑之类的。

cues.en: Remember when Microsoft changed office to the ribbon menu and everyone kind of freaked out because it didn't use the old menu bar convention, so it acted and operated differently from every other application that was on Windows?
cues.zh: 还记得微软把 Office 改成 Ribbon 菜单时，大家都炸锅了吗？因为它没有沿用旧的菜单栏惯例，所以它的行为和操作方式跟 Windows 上其他所有应用都不一样。

cues.en: See, that's an example of broken continuity.
cues.zh: 你看，这就是连续性被破坏的一个例子。

cues.en: Now eventually, we all kinda got used to it and it wasn't too far a departure from the old user interface, so we all kinda learned to live with it. Plus, at least within the Office Suite, there was continuity in the new ribbon interface.
cues.zh: 后来，大家慢慢也就习惯了，而且它跟旧界面差别不算太大，所以也就学着接受了。再说，至少在 Office 套件里，新的 Ribbon 界面还是保持了连续性。

cues.en: And there are even some advantages, although honestly, I still prefer the old Office menu interface.
cues.zh: 甚至还有一些优点，不过说实话，我还是更喜欢旧的 Office 菜单界面。

cues.en: Anyway, that's digressing. Point is companies that make operating systems publish detailed
cues.zh: 总之，扯远了。重点是，做操作系统的公司会发布详细的

cues.en: specific reports on exactly
cues.zh: 具体报告，精确说明

cues.en: how people should design third party application user interfaces.
cues.zh: 人们应该如何设计第三方应用的用户界面。

cues.en: These are called human interface guidelines.
cues.zh: 这些叫做人机界面指南。

cues.en: They're all designed to make sure that continuity is maintained, that doing one thing in one app will do the same thing in another app.
cues.zh: 它们的目的都是确保一致性，让在一个应用里做某件事的方式，在另一个应用里也相同。

cues.en: Apple's got one for Mac and another one for iOS.
cues.zh: Apple 有一套给 Mac 的，还有一套给 iOS 的。

cues.en: Google's got one for Android,
cues.zh: Google 有一套给 Android 的，

cues.en: and Microsoft has one for Windows, except that Microsoft apparently threw all that out when they designed Windows eight.
cues.zh: Microsoft 也有一套给 Windows 的，只不过 Microsoft 在设计 Windows 8 时显然把这些全抛掉了。

cues.en: So they just stapled the Metro user interface with one set of user interface guidelines over the desktop
cues.zh: 所以他们就把遵循一套界面指南的 Metro 用户界面，硬生生地盖在了桌面上

cues.en: with a completely different set of guidelines.
cues.zh: 而桌面遵循的是完全不同的一套指南。

cues.en: So when you do this, how can you expect to have continuity?
cues.zh: 那么当你这样做时，又怎能指望保持连续性？

cues.en: The answer is you can't, which brings me to my final point, context.
cues.zh: 答案是不能，这就引出了我的最后一点：上下文。

cues.en: One of the smartest things Microsoft has ever done, maybe even the smartest thing Microsoft has ever done,
cues.zh: 微软做过的最聪明的事情之一，也许甚至是微软做过的最聪明的事情，

cues.en: was back when they designed Windows 95,
cues.zh: 是在他们设计 Windows 95 的时候，

cues.en: they knew it would be a new user interface. They knew people wouldn't know what to do with it at first. So they put the word start on the button that opened the start menu.
cues.zh: 他们知道这会是一个全新的用户界面。他们知道人们一开始会不知道怎么用。于是他们在打开开始菜单的按钮上写了 Start。

cues.en: Don't know where to start? Well, right there. It tells you. Start there. Press that button to do something. I mean, seems kinda obvious, but, really, I guarantee that there were high level meetings within Microsoft deciding what that button should say at anything. Should it be a blank, just an icon? Should it say run or begin or first or... No. Start. It's the start button. It starts things, and it was a good move.
cues.zh: 不知道从哪儿开始？喏，就在那儿。它会告诉你。就从那儿开始。按下那个按钮，就能做点什么。我是说，看起来挺明显的，但我保证，微软内部开过高管会议，专门决定那个按钮上到底该写什么。是留空，还是只放个图标？该写“运行”“开始”“第一个”还是……不。开始。这是开始按钮。它能启动各种东西，而且这步走得对。

cues.en: They stuck with that from Windows 90 five all the way to Windows XP.
cues.zh: 他们从 Windows 95 一直沿用到 Windows XP。

cues.en: The first Windows not to use the start label on the start menu was Vista. And personally, even though I think that was a bit of a mistake, by then we were all kinda used to the concept of the start menu being the button in the lower left hand corner, so it wasn't that big a deal.
cues.zh: 第一个不在开始菜单上使用 Start 标签的 Windows 是 Vista。就我个人而言，虽然我觉得那算是个小失误，但那时大家已经有点习惯开始菜单就是左下角那个按钮的概念了，所以也没多大关系。

cues.en: In Windows eight, nothing's labeled.
cues.zh: 到了 Windows 8，什么标签都没有了。

cues.en: First, they got rid of the start menu and replaced it with something... Well, it may say start, but it's decidedly not the start menu.
cues.zh: 首先，他们去掉了开始菜单，换成了个……嗯，它可能写着 Start，但绝对不是开始菜单。

cues.en: You can't just start any application from the new start thing, which I'm just gonna call the task panel.
cues.zh: 你不能直接从那个新的“开始”玩意儿里启动任意应用，我就管它叫任务面板。

cues.en: See, you have your tasks on there. It's a panel instead of a task bar,
cues.zh: 你看，你的任务都在上面。它是面板，不是任务栏，

cues.en: task panel.
cues.zh: 任务面板。

cues.en: That would have made a hell of a lot more sense than calling it start
cues.zh: 这么叫可比叫“开始”合理多了

cues.en: because
cues.zh: 因为

cues.en: task panel
cues.zh: 任务面板

cues.en: describes what the hell it does.
cues.zh: 才说清了它到底干什么。

cues.en: Additionally, while we're on the subject, the charms bar.
cues.zh: 另外，既然说到这个，还有 Charms 栏。

cues.en: What exactly makes it the charms bar? Is it the home of a little leprechaun?
cues.zh: 到底是什么让它成了 Charms 栏？里面住着个小矮妖吗？

cues.en: Ee, I'm the Windows eight leprechaun.
cues.zh: 呃，我是 Windows 8 小妖精。

cues.en: I'm after me gold.
cues.zh: 我在找我的金子。

cues.en: No. No. No. No. Just...
cues.zh: 不。不。不。不。只是……

cues.en: No. Look. One of the things that make an operating system user friendly is that it provides enough context to make sense of the user interface.
cues.zh: 不。你看，操作系统之所以用户友好，其中一个原因就是它提供了足够的上下文，让用户能理解界面。

cues.en: Sometimes that's words in the right places. Sometimes it's a little thing like the bulging of the Macintosh trash can when there's files ready to be deleted or the fact that my computer
cues.zh: 有时是出现在正确位置上的文字；有时只是个小细节，比如有文件待删除时 Macintosh 废纸篓会鼓起来，或者我的电脑

cues.en: looks like a computer.
cues.zh: 看起来像一台电脑。

cues.en: Indeed, we're starting to get into a weird area where the icons we use, like the floppy disk for save and the rotary phone for dial,
cues.zh: 确实，我们开始进入一个奇怪的领域：我们用的图标，比如代表保存的软盘、代表拨号的旋转式电话，

cues.en: were based on physical things which have long since passed into obsolescence.
cues.zh: 都基于早已被淘汰的实体物品。

cues.en: Yet they've become part of our cultural context and we can't really change them.
cues.zh: 但它们已经成为我们文化语境的一部分，我们没法真正改变它们。

cues.en: Ideally,
cues.zh: 理想情况下，

cues.en: we should be able at a glance to understand what these things are and what they're able to do.
cues.zh: 我们应该一眼就能看懂这些图标是什么、能做什么。

cues.en: That's why icons need to be non confusing.
cues.zh: 所以图标不能让人困惑。

cues.en: I mean, going back to the word start, the reason that they included it in Windows '90 five was because we needed that context.
cues.zh: 我是说，回到“开始”这个词，他们把它放进 Windows 95 的原因是我们需要那个上下文。

cues.en: By the time they removed it, we were already familiar enough with the idea of a start menu that we no longer needed that context clue. So it was okay.
cues.zh: 等他们把它去掉的时候，我们已经对开始菜单这个概念足够熟悉，不再需要那个上下文线索了。所以没问题。

cues.en: This goes even further
cues.zh: 这还能更进一步

cues.en: when you realize that many of the applications in the metro interface use high resolution pictures, but don't actually make clear the name of the application in the application itself.
cues.zh: 当你意识到 Metro 界面里的很多应用都用高分辨率图片，却并没有在应用本身里明确写出应用的名称时。

cues.en: If it even mentions the application name, it'll be in very small text. So not only is it hard to tell at a glance what does what in the metro interface,
cues.zh: 即使提到了应用名称，文字也会非常小。所以在地铁界面里不仅一眼很难看出哪个是干什么的，

cues.en: but it's not very information dense. That is, you don't get a lot of information from a little bit of effort.
cues.zh: 而且信息密度也不高。也就是说，你不用费多少力气，但也得不到多少信息。

cues.en: Another thing you might wanna think about, there's absolutely no indication which items in the Windows eight interface are clickable and what's just decoration.
cues.zh: 另外你可能会想到的一点是，Windows 8 界面里完全没有提示哪些项目是可以点击的，哪些只是装饰。

cues.en: Take a web browser for example. You can immediately see what items are hyperlinks
cues.zh: 以网页浏览器为例，你一眼就能看出哪些条目是超链接

cues.en: because they're different in some way.
cues.zh: 因为它们在某种程度上有所不同。

cues.en: Now there's many ways to accomplish this. They may be a different color or they may be bolder or they may be underlined
cues.zh: 实现这一点有很多方式。它们可能颜色不同，可能更粗，也可能带下划线

cues.en: or they may be bold... A different color and underlined.
cues.zh: 或者可能加粗……颜色不同还带下划线。

cues.en: Anyway, if there's a program user interface, something may be on top of a button or cast a little shadow,
cues.zh: 总之，在程序用户界面里，某个元素可能浮在按钮上方，或投下一点阴影，

cues.en: these differences create context that separates the interactive items from the static items.
cues.zh: 这些差异营造出上下文，把可交互条目和静态条目区分开。

cues.en: Windows eight doesn't have that. Icons don't have borders, shading,
cues.zh: Windows 8 没有这些。图标没有边框、没有阴影，

cues.en: they're not on little buttons, they're just there, and they're not any different from anything else by any context.
cues.zh: 它们不在小按钮上，就是直接摆在那儿，而且无论从什么语境看，它们跟别的东西都没什么区别。

cues.en: Finally, and this just may be me in my opinion here, but the human eye tends to appreciate white space.
cues.zh: 最后，这可能只是我个人的看法，但人眼往往偏爱留白。

cues.en: We don't want our icons clumped together and the square on square interface in Metro may look modern,
cues.zh: 我们不希望图标挤成一团，而 Metro 里方块叠方块的界面也许看起来现代，

cues.en: but it doesn't look comfortable.
cues.zh: 但看起来并不舒服。

cues.en: It's hard to explain, but it's kinda like the difference between living in Frank Lloyd Wright's falling water house and Pruitt ego.
cues.zh: 这很难解释，但有点像住在 Frank Lloyd Wright 的 Fallingwater 和 Pruitt-Igoe 之间的区别。

cues.en: Oh, I forgot. Not everyone took that elective in modern architecture. Sorry. Okay. It's the difference between flying coach and flying first class. There's just more elbow room. So anyway, that's just what I found I had problems with. And that was just in the first thirty freaking minutes. I mean, I literally could not take it anymore. It was like torture.
cues.zh: 哦，我忘了。不是每个人都选修过现代建筑课。抱歉。好吧。这就像坐经济舱和坐头等舱的区别。就是活动空间更大。总之，这就是我觉得有问题的地方。而且那还只是在前该死的三十分钟里。我是说，我真的受不了了。那简直像酷刑。

cues.en: I'm not kidding. I wanted to scream, and the only reason I didn't was because I was in the middle of a coffee shop when I was reviewing this.
cues.zh: 我没开玩笑。我当时真想尖叫，唯一没叫出声的原因，是我评审这段的时候正坐在咖啡店里。

cues.en: So that's my take. Hey. But what do I know? I'm just a tech geek. It's not like I'm a usability expert,
cues.zh: 这就是我的看法。嘿，但我又懂什么呢？我只是个技术极客。我又不是什么可用性专家，

cues.en: analyst group focusing on user experience.
cues.zh: 专门研究用户体验的分析师团队。

cues.en: And she said that Windows eight is optimized for content consumption rather than content production and multitasking.
cues.zh: 她说 Windows 8 是为内容消费优化的，而不是为了内容创作和多任务处理。

cues.en: Whereas content consumption can easily be done on other media such as tablets and phones,
cues.zh: 内容消费可以轻松地在平板和手机等其他设备上完成，

cues.en: production production and multitasking are still best suited for PCs.
cues.zh: 内容生产与多任务处理仍然最适合在 PC 上进行。

cues.en: Windows eight seems to ignore that.
cues.zh: Windows 8 似乎忽略了这一点。

cues.en: Also, at Nielsen Norman Group, the cofounder Jacob Nielsen said,
cues.zh: 另外，Nielsen Norman Group 的联合创始人 Jacob Nielsen 说，

cues.en: one of the worst aspects of Windows eight is that the product's very name has become a misnomer.
cues.zh: Windows 8 最糟糕的方面之一是，这个产品的名字本身已经名不副实。

cues.en: Windows no longer supports multiple windows on the screen. The product ought to be renamed Microsoft Window.
cues.zh: Windows 已不再支持屏幕上多个窗口。这个产品应该改名为 Microsoft Window。

cues.en: Maybe I wouldn't be so pissed off about this if Microsoft still supported sales of Windows seven.
cues.zh: 如果微软还支持销售 Windows 7，也许我就不会这么恼火了。

cues.en: Maybe if they let the market choose instead of trying to impose this new operating system from the top down, but you can't find new copies of Windows seven at Staples or anything, you don't get a choice what OS your computer is installed with. It's not just a bad operating system. It's a bad operating system Microsoft is pretty much forcing on new PC users.
cues.zh: 也许如果他们让市场来选择，而不是自上而下强推这个新操作系统，可你在 Staples 之类的地方根本买不到新的 Windows 7 拷贝，你也没法选择电脑预装什么操作系统。这不只是一个糟糕的操作系统。这是微软几乎强加给新 PC 用户的糟糕操作系统。

cues.en: And personally, I think it's bad enough that it warrants a product recall.
cues.zh: 我个人觉得，这已经严重到该召回产品了。

cues.en: I mean, it's that defective.
cues.zh: 我是说，它缺陷就是这么严重。

cues.en: How did this product get approved?
cues.zh: 这产品怎么通过审批的？

cues.en: How did it get released?
cues.zh: 怎么发布出去的？

cues.en: Who signed off on this? Because honestly, they should be so horribly horribly fired.
cues.zh: 这是谁签字批准的？说实话，他们真该被狠狠炒掉。

cues.en: Their employee ID card should be hung on pikes outside of Microsoft's Redmond HQ
cues.zh: 他们的工牌应该被挂在微软雷德蒙德总部外的长矛上

cues.en: as a reminder to anyone else who perpetrates such stupidity.
cues.zh: 好警示其他任何犯这种蠢的人。

cues.en: And I'd include Balmer on that list.
cues.zh: 我也会把 Balmer 算进这份名单。

cues.en: Anyway, that's my take on Windows eight.
cues.zh: 总之，这就是我对 Windows 8 的看法。
